findings: Actual unchanged CLI reports distinct unreadable same-size files as duplicates: failed ifstream read hashes empty data without error.
File sizes narrow into int keys;1and2^32+1share bucket key on tested host. Size bucket ordering can interleave actual sizes; full multi-GB CLI miss not tested.

Digest-table hasher collapses65536distinct explicit keys into256hash outputs. Full digest key equality still distinguishes bucket collisions; this is performance weakness, not a demonstrated SHA1 collision.
SHA1 maxlen helper may read full8192-byte block beyond a shorter requested prefix. Normal64KiBprefix is block-aligned.
Cached hashes remain stale after content changes; no final source verification.
Computing fullhash on a copied file_info does not retain that cache in stored entry; repeated comparisons can reread contents.
Four equal files emit all six pair edges; physical hardlink aliases reported as duplicate path pair.
Initial documented Boost.System link flag fails on installed header-only Boost.System. Removing only obsolete link flag builds unchanged C++11 source against real Boost.Filesystem/OpenSSL.
Source accepts SHA1 match without direct byte confirmation; no source/error/cancellation/resource admission guards.
limits: Five pinned repository files read and exact Git blob hashes verified. Fifteen original-function/actual CLI controls on synthetic local files; dependencies/link flags documented. No actual SHA1 collision, large sparse-file CLI, measured throughput, source concurrency stress or cross-platform qualification. README external benchmark image/figures not independently qualified.
